question: Where can I get the current electricity network access tariffs and charges in the United States, by voltage level and period, with their history?

answer.summary: There is no single national table. Transmission access rates are FERC-filed tariffs (eTariff, XML export, versions since 2010) and RTOs post computed rates: PJM zonal NITS in $/MW-year (XLSX), CAISO high/low-voltage access charges in $/MWh (PDF). Distribution charges are in each utility's state-approved tariff, e.g. Oncor (TX) by secondary/primary/transmission service and PG&E (CA) with distribution and transmission components by voltage and TOU period. OpenEI URDB compiles rates nationally but is mostly bundled retail rates.
main_caveats: Transmission (FERC, wholesale) and distribution (state commissions, retail) are regulated separately; no source covers both nationally.
In vertically integrated states retail tariffs are bundled; a network-only charge may not exist as a published value.
Units differ: PJM $/MW-year, CAISO $/MWh, utility tariffs $/kW, $/kWh and $/customer; do not compare without conversion rules.
URDB is a convenience compilation; its voltage tags and start dates can differ from the official tariff.
answer.confidence_reason: Sources tested with downloads, but distribution tariffs and RTO postings were sampled (3 utilities, 2 RTOs); PUCT summary blocked to automated clients.

attributes.note: Transmission: eTariff and RTO postings (PJM, CAISO tested). Distribution: per-utility tariffs, sampled Oncor, PG&E, Con Edison.
attributes.gap_note: No national official compilation found (FERC, PUCT, OpenEI checked). Distribution tariffs tested for 3 utilities only; MISO, SPP, ISO-NE, NYISO postings and other states not opened.

attributes.note: Components separated in sample: PG&E unbundles distribution/transmission; Oncor delivery charges plus TCRF/DCRF riders; CAISO HV/LV TAC.
attributes.gap_note: Separation of network charges was checked only in the sampled tariffs; bundled-rate utilities were not examined individually.

attributes.note: CAISO HV (>=200 kV) vs LV; PG&E and Oncor secondary/primary/transmission service; PJM NITS has no voltage split.
attributes.gap_note: Voltage classes verified in 3 utility tariffs and CAISO only; URDB voltagecategory is empty in 44,320 of 58,920 rows and can contradict the rate name.

attributes.note: PG&E B-19 peak 4-9 p.m., part-peak, off-peak, summer Jun-Sep; Oncor distribution and PJM/CAISO transmission rates have no time bands.
attributes.gap_note: Time-of-use definitions read in PG&E B-19 only; other utilities' calendars not checked (URDB holds 12x24 schedules but unverified).
Latest versions identified only for the tested sources; each other utility or RTO must be checked separately.

sources.name: eTariff Viewer (tariffs filed with FERC, including Open Access Transmission Tariffs)
sources.format: HTML viewer; XML export per tariff (eTariff export schema); RTF/PDF print
sources.adds: The legally filed text of every FERC-jurisdictional transmission tariff (OATT rate schedules, formula-rate attachments, interconnection and wheeling rates) with section-level version history since electronic filing started in 2010.
sources.summary: FERC's official register of filed tariffs: every FERC-jurisdictional OATT and transmission rate schedule, with section versions and effective dates; XML export per tariff.
sources.coverage_note: Wholesale/interstate transmission service. Not retail distribution tariffs (state PUCs) and not ERCOT-internal utilities.
caveats: Rates are inside tariff text, not typed fields; formula rates need the RTO's posted results.
ferc.gov pages refuse automated clients; etariff.ferc.gov works.

coverage.geographic: United States: wholesale/interstate transmission tariffs of FERC-jurisdictional public utilities, RTO/ISOs and federal power administrations. ERCOT-only utilities and most retail distribution tariffs are not filed here.

attempts.note: The XML export carries tariff text (record_plain_text) and status/dates, not typed rate fields; units appear only inside the tariff text of each rate schedule.

inclusion_rule.value: Tariffs and tariff revisions of public utilities, gas and oil pipelines and power administrations filed electronically since 2010-10-01 (Order No. 714).
inclusion_rule.quote: Order No. 714, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission revised its regulations to require that, effective October 1, 2010, all tariffs and tariff revisions and rate change applications for the public utilities, natural gas pipelines, oil pipelines and power administrations be filed electronically

reference_date.value: Each tariff record carries its own effective date and status; the export is stamped with tariff_export_date (2026-11-26T09:33Z in the test).

update_frequency.value: Continuous: records change whenever a filing is accepted; no publisher-stated schedule found.

attempts.note: Guide (July 2025) describes statuses and history but states no update schedule.

exclusions.value: The viewer rendition is not the legal filed rate; Commission orders control.
exclusions.quote: The rendition of the tariff provisions and the status of these provisions is based on the best efforts of Commission staff, but does not necessarily represent the rates or terms and conditions of service on file at any particular point in time.

key_fields.meaning: Tariff section title and number, e.g. OATT SCHEDULE 7, OATT Attachment H-1
Version of the section (e.g. 15.0.1); history of versions is shown in the viewer
Effective, Accepted, Suspended, Pending, Conditionally Accepted/Effective, Tolled
Legal validity of the record, distinct from tariff time-of-use periods
Text of the section, where rate values and units appear
Filing and order that put the record in place

how_to_use.example_request: curl -s -c cj -b cj https://etariff.ferc.gov/TariffExport.aspx?tid=1763 > page.html; then POST the page's hidden ASP.NET fields plus __EVENTTARGET=ctl00$Content1$btnExport, ctl00$Content1$lstStatus$0=9 (Effective), ctl00$Content1$lstBinaryText$1=2 (plain text) to the same URL with the same cookies
how_to_use.example_result: 200 application/octet-stream, Content-Disposition: attachment;filename=Tariff_1763.xml, 1,260,358 bytes; <tariff_title>Interregional Agreements</tariff_title>; 292 record_data elements, first: record_content_desc 19.1, record_version_num 0.0.0
steps: On TariffList.aspx choose the program 'Electric TCS and MBR' or type a company name (e.g. PJM) and click Find Tariffs; each row gives TariffBrowser.aspx?tid=<id> (sections and history) and TariffExport.aspx?tid=<id> (XML).
For an RTO OATT, rate values sit in schedules and attachments (e.g. PJM OATT Schedule 7, Schedule 8, Attachment H-1 ... H-xx); open the section to see its version history.
For a dated view use the date box in TariffBrowser (sections effective on that date) or the RTF/PDF print link TariffPrint.aspx?tid=<id>&date=MMDDYYYY.
Parse the XML with the namespace http://ferc.gov/etariffExport.xsd; rate tables must be read from record_plain_text.
reading_traps: The XML export only covers the statuses ticked in the dialog; the default is Effective, so superseded versions need the viewer history or other statuses.
Formula-rate tariffs (e.g. PJM Attachment H) hold the formula; the resulting annual revenue requirement and $/MW-year rate are posted by the RTO, not as a field in eTariff.
ASP.NET postbacks: section clicks in TariffBrowser need valid view state; a stale postback returned HTTP 302 in the test.

problems: www.ferc.gov and ferc.gov return a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' 403 page to non-browser clients; the etariff.ferc.gov application itself answered normally.
Queries require ASP.NET form posts (view state); there is no documented public API.

steps: PJM: open the XLSX, one sheet per validity period; zones with several owners have the zonal total and rate on a separate row below the owner rows.
CAISO: open the latest revision on the yearly library page; page 1 has the HV TAC rate, later pages the HV/LV components per transmission owner with TRR effective date and docket.
Use the yearly archive pages for history (CAISO from 2008-2011; PJM annual files 2021-2025 and 2026 dated files).
reading_traps: CAISO republishes the same effective date with revisions: the Jun 01, 2026 ISO HV TAC rate was 15.8352 $/MWh in an earlier version and 15.8508 $/MWh in the revision dated Sep 09, 2026 (R7).
PJM's PDF has no period heading in its text layer; the period appears in the XLSX sheet names and in a footnote ('As of 10/1/2026').
PJM rates are annual demand rates ($/MW-Year), not energy rates; they are not differentiated by voltage or time of day.
Several PJM zones (ATSI, DAYTON, EKPC, PPL) were revised retroactively to June 1, 2026 by FERC directive, so earlier 2026 files differ.

steps: Identify the distribution utility serving the area and its state commission.
Download the current tariff book and find the schedule for the customer class; Oncor lists delivery schedules under 6.1.1.1, PG&E publishes one PDF per schedule.
Read the voltage columns and TOU period definitions in the same schedule; for unbundled components use PG&E's 'UNBUNDLING OF TOTAL RATES' sheet or Oncor's riders (TCRF, DCRF).

For history use the utility's historic rate files (PG&E: XLSX per validity period; Commercial B schedules from November 1, 2019, residential baseline from July 15, 1993) or the commission's tariff filings.
reading_traps: PG&E's historic XLSX files give total bundled rates; the network components (distribution, transmission) only appear in the PDF unbundling sheet.
Oncor's tariff PDF mixes sheets with different effective dates (e.g. June 1, 2026 and January 15, 2015); read the date on each sheet.
In Texas the delivery charge is billed through the retail electric provider; supply prices are not in the TDU tariff.
Con Edison's website copies are convenience copies; the company says official leaves with receipt stamps are those on file with the NYPSC.

problems: The Texas PUCT site (puc.texas.gov, ftp.puc.texas.gov) returned a Cloudflare block (403) to non-browser requests; the summary of TDU charges was read only through an archived copy of 2024-10-27.

steps: Download the bulk CSV (12.2 MB gz, 737 columns, 58,920 rows on 2026-11-26) or use the API (version 7, free api.data.gov key).
Each row is a rate version; group by eiaid and name, and use startdate/enddate/supersedes to build history.
Use servicetype to separate Delivery-only rates (3,252 rows) from Bundled rates (10,039 rows); most rows leave it empty.
Check each value against the 'source' tariff before use.
reading_traps: voltagecategory can contradict the rate name: PG&E 'B-19 ... (Transmission) Mandatory' is tagged Secondary.
URDB startdate (2026-03-27) differs from the tariff effective date (March 1, 2026) for PG&E B-19.
30,852 rows have no enddate, including rates last started in 2014 (e.g. Oncor POLR rows), so 'no enddate' is not 'currently effective'.
The wiki states 'over 3,700 U.S. utilities' while the approved-rate download has 2,843 distinct eiaid values; the definitions were not reconciled.
Most rows are total retail rates, not network access charges.
